title: Lensless Fluorescent Microscopy on a Chip
protocol: Mix PDMS A and B elastomers with a 1:10 volume ratio.
Pour the mixed solution into a Petri dish.
Cure the mixture at 65 °C for 2 hours.
Extract the required size and shape of the micro-fluidic channel wall from the Petri dish using an X-acto knife.
Expose both the cover glass slides and PDMS bonding area with a high-frequency plasma generator.
Place the device inside an oven for 40-50 minutes at 70 °C to strengthen the bonding.
Remove the cover glass of the opto-electronic sensor-array.
Gently place a thin absorption filter on top of the detector active area using a vacuum pen.
Position a fiber-optic faceplate or taper on top of the absorption filter.
Directly place the fabricated micro-fluidic chip on top of the fiber-optic array.
Assemble a glass prism or hemi-sphere above the micro-fluidic chip using index-matching oil.
Move side illumination fiber closer to the prism (or hemisphere) and adjust its angle for total-internal reflection.
Align vertical illumination perpendicular to the detector-array and center it to the desired field-of-view.
Turn on/off side and vertical light-sources sequentially to achieve both fluorescent imaging and bright-field transmission imaging.
Acquire lensfree raw images using a custom-developed Labview interface through a PC.
Combine raw fluorescent bead solutions with DI water to optimize sample concentration.
Mix 10 μL of fluorescent bead solution with 40 μL, 5 mL, and 20 mL of DI water for 10 μm, 4 μm, and 2 μm diameter beads, respectively.
Mix different bead solutions to prepare heterogeneous solutions as needed.
Inject the final sample solution into the micro-fluidic chip using a sharp syringe needle from the side PDMS walls.
Mix ~100 μL whole blood with ~1 mL of red blood cell lysing buffer.
Incubate the mixture for ~3 min.
Centrifuge the lysed blood solution and resuspend the pellet layer in ~200 μL of PBS.
Add 5 μL of 1 mM SYTO 16 to the 200 μL resuspension.
Incubate the sample in dark at room temperature for ~30 min.
Centrifuge the labeled sample again and remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the white blood cell pellet layer in PBS.
Transfer the resuspended cells to a micro-fluidic chip for lensfree on-chip fluorescent imaging.
Process lensless fluorescent images using Lucy-Richardson deconvolution algorithm.
Apply compressive sampling based decoding algorithm to increase resolution.
Quantify resolution enhancement by resolving closely packed bead-pairs.
Pseudocolor reconstructed lensfree fluorescent images if desired.
Use custom-developed algorithms requiring only a CPU for digital processing.
Consider using GPUs for faster processing if necessary.
Automatically count decoded fluorescent objects using custom interface if needed.
Estimate the incoherent point-spread function of the on-chip system.
Create several measured lensfree fluorescent patterns using isolated small fluorescent beads.
Align individual fluorescent patterns with respect to their center of mass coordinates.
Normalize the aligned patterns for appropriate intensity.
Average the normalized patterns to obtain the point-spread function.
Use the averaged pattern as the fluorescent point-spread function for the on-chip microscope.
Feed raw acquired fluorescent images and measured point-spread function into an accelerated Lucy-Richardson algorithm.
Apply Bayes' theorem in the Lucy-Richardson algorithm to refine maximum-likelihood estimation of fluorescence source distribution.
Iterate the refinement process until minimal square error between projected and measured lensfree patterns is achieved.
Terminate iterations before noise amplification occurs, typically after a few hundred cycles.
Accelerate convergence of the deconvolution algorithm using vector extrapolation method.
